_comment: The stage-1 baseline and the selector's inertness control, in one pass
navigation.kind is "input" because there is nothing to pin in the
`baseline` half: the whole point of the pair is that one arm carries no
cheat at all. The `control` half carries `cheat=0030:00` - the selector
pinned at the value stage 1 already is - so the two arms differ in exactly
one thing, and s3's test applies: the pin is inert when the two
This is NOT a navigation sweep and not a rung: it reaches one place, the
place the game goes on its own. It lives beside navigation.json because
the baseline it records is a required half of ADR-0239 s5's metric, and
the sweep is run with `--baseline runs/f1418/lifeforce/before/baseline`.
Run it with the same command as the sweep, at 120 s:

navigation.label: stage selector held at its stage-1 value
navigation.source: Almar's Guides, Life Force Action Replay Codes (USA) (almarsguides.com/retro/walkthroughs/nes/games/LifeForce/ActionReplay/): "Stage Select - Stage 1/Cell Stage:  0030:00". DataCrystal's Life Force (NES)/RAM map (datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Life_Force/RAM_map) lists the byte as "0x0030  ??? (Linked to stage, music theme?)" without a value table. The value 00 is stage 1, which is where the game loads without a selector at all, so pinning it there is the one configuration in which a difference between the arms could only be the pin's.
